summary: You take the twelve first-year core courses for a letter grade, STATS 319 and STATS 390 twice each, and depth (three advanced STATS courses) and breadth (three courses outside Statistics) courses totaling 24 units, toward 135 units. The qualifying exams, the dissertation proposal meeting, four quarters of teaching, candidacy, your 3.0 GPA, the oral exam and the dissertation are checked by hand.

children.name: Depth Requirement
children.notes: Students must complete a depth requirement consisting of a minimum of three courses (minimum nine units) of advanced topics courses offered by the department. Courses may be taken for a letter grade or credit. Courses for the depth and breadth requirements must equal a combined minimum of 24 units, i.e. the final two courses (minimum six units) can be either depth or breadth. Recommended advanced topics courses include, but are not limited to, those listed above.

children.name: Breadth Requirement
children.notes:
Students must take at least three courses (minimum nine units) outside the department. Courses may be taken for a letter grade or credit. They are advised to choose an area of concentration in a specific scientific field of statistical applications approved by their PhD program advisor. Courses for the depth and breadth requirements must equal a combined minimum of 24 units units, i.e. the final two courses (minimum six units) can be either depth or breadth.
Popular areas include Computational Biology and Statistical Genomics, Machine Learning, Applied Probability, Earth Science Statistics, and Social and Behavioral Sciences.
